title: Airworthiness Directives; Pilatus Aircraft Ltd. Airplanes
summary: The FAA is superseding Airworthiness Directive (AD) 2021-11- 08, which applied to all Pilatus Aircraft Ltd. (Pilatus) Model PC-6, PC-6-H1, PC-6-H2, PC-6/350, PC-6/350-H1, PC-6/350-H2, PC-6/A, PC-6/A- H1, PC-6/A-H2, PC-6/B-H2, PC-6/B1-H2, PC-6/B2-H2, PC-6/B2-H4, PC-6/C- H2, and PC-6/C1-H2 airplanes. AD 2021-11-08 required revising the airworthiness limitations section (ALS) of the existing aircraft maintenance manual (AMM) or instructions for continued airworthiness (ICA) to incorporate new airworthiness limitations and adding an additional eddy current inspection of the fuselage wing fittings and wing-to-fuselage fittings if the last inspection was performed using an earlier version of the required material. Since the FAA issued AD 2021- 11-08, the FAA has determined that new or more restrictive airworthiness limitations are necessary. This AD requires revising the ALS of the existing AMM or ICA for these airplanes. The FAA is issuing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

title: Airworthiness Directives; Airbus Canada Limited Partnership (Type Certificate Previously Held by C Series Aircraft Limited Partnership (CSALP); Bombardier, Inc.) Airplanes
summary: The FAA is adopting a new airworthiness directive (AD) for certain Airbus Canada Limited Partnership Model BD-500-1A10 and BD-500- 1A11 airplanes. This AD was prompted by a report of multiple in-service failures of pressure regulating shutoff valves (PRSOVs). This AD requires revising the existing airplane flight manual (AFM) to incorporate procedures for reducing the thrust lever or shutting down the engine when the BLEED LEAK caution message is persistent, prohibits operation in known or forecasted icing conditions under certain minimum equipment list (MEL) provisions where the only operative PRSOV is an affected part, and requires replacement of affected PRSOVs with improved PRSOVs. The FAA is issuing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

title: Thresholds Increase for the Major Assets Prohibition of the Depository Institution Management Interlocks Act Rule
summary: The NCUA Board (Board) is issuing a final rule increasing two thresholds in its regulation implementing management official interlocks for purposes of the Depository Institution Management Interlocks Act (DIMIA). DIMIA authorizes NCUA to adjust the major assets prohibition thresholds through regulation to respond to inflation or market changes. This final rule increases both major assets prohibition thresholds to $10 billion to account for changes in the United States banking market since 1996. Additionally, the final rule removes a presumption related to depository institutions controlled or managed by persons who are members of a minority group or women.

title: Corporate Credit Unions
summary: The NCUA Board (Board) is amending its regulations for corporate credit unions by removing the requirement that a corporate credit union's asset and liability management committee (ALCO) must have at least one member who is also a member of the corporate credit union's board of directors. The final rule also removes filing requirements related to a corporate credit union's annual report and any management letter or other report issued by its independent public accountant. The intended effect is to reduce unnecessary regulatory burden and provide corporate credit unions with greater flexibility.
